note: Held-out corpus for ProseShape 1.4.2, written and frozen on 2026-10-05 before any 1.4.2 change and never used for iteration. It is weighted toward the gap the 1.4.1 validation found, over-editing writing a person already wrote well: six real human excerpts and four near-clean human-style texts, against six AI-shaped texts that check for regressions. m01-m10 are synthetic; every name, organization, address, phone number and figure in them is fictional. m11-m16 are human-written excerpts (sources and licenses below and in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md). None of the texts overlap ProseShape's fixtures, examples, or earlier corpora.
user_request: Please humanize this so it reads like a person wrote it. Keep the facts and meaning the same.

sources.m11_human_thoreau: Henry David Thoreau, Walden (1854), 'The Pond in Winter', second paragraph. Public domain. Project Gutenberg #205. Line breaks unwrapped.
sources.m12_human_chesterton: G. K. Chesterton, 'On Running After One's Hat', All Things Considered (1908). Public domain. Project Gutenberg #11505. Two paragraphs, line breaks unwrapped.
sources.m13_human_lincoln: Abraham Lincoln, letter to Horace Greeley, 22 August 1862, as printed in Speeches & Letters of Abraham Lincoln, 1832-1865 (Everyman edition). Public domain. Project Gutenberg #14721. Line breaks unwrapped; Gutenberg's _italics_ converted to *asterisks* and -- to an em dash.
sources.m14_human_eisenhower: Dwight D. Eisenhower, Farewell Address, 17 January 1961. A work of the US government, public domain. Transcript from the National Archives (archives.gov, Milestone Documents). Two transcription errors corrected against the delivered text: hyphens around 'economic, political, even spiritual' restored as dashes, and 'United State corporations' as 'United States corporations'.
sources.m15_human_kubernetes: Kubernetes documentation, 'Overview' (kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/overview/), section 'Why you need Kubernetes and what it can do'. The Kubernetes Authors, CC BY 4.0. HTML converted to Markdown; the first four list items.
sources.m16_human_go_errors: Damien Neil and Jonathan Amsterdam, 'Working with Errors in Go 1.13', The Go Blog, 17 October 2019 (go.dev/blog/go1.13-errors). Text CC BY 4.0, code BSD. Opening paragraphs; HTML converted to Markdown.

m01_talk_abstract.category: conference talk abstract (title, bullet list, speaker line)
m01_talk_abstract.expected: cut the inflated opener and closer; keep every figure, tool, service count, bullet and the speaker details

m02_real_estate_listing.category: real estate listing (address, specs, price, open house, agent)
m02_real_estate_listing.expected: plain and still selling; keep every spec, figure, date, and the agent's details

m03_museum_label.category: museum wall text (tombstone lines, italic title, significance closer)
m03_museum_label.expected: keep the tombstone lines exactly, every fact and the technique; cut the significance commentary or keep its claim plainly

m04_hr_policy_email.category: HR policy email (bold-label lists, dates, figures)
m04_hr_policy_email.expected: cut chatbot courtesies and commitment boilerplate; keep every rule, date, figure and the list structure

m05_travel_itinerary.expected: cut the hype; keep the headings, every price, time, distance and tip

m06_scifi_scene.category: science fiction scene (stock sensations, thesis dialogue, realization)
m06_scifi_scene.expected: rewrite mode: keep every beat, both positions, the decision and the ending; tighten stock sensations and the stated realization without inventing actions

m07_nearclean_review.expected: few or no changes; every figure, quirk, and the verdict stay in the writer's words
protected: hold the minus button for five seconds
Would I buy it again? Yes.

m08_nearclean_school_email.category: near-clean human-style teacher email with one stock triad
m08_nearclean_school_email.expected: minimal edit; logistics exact; the triad may be lightly plainer but the warm close and the octopus line stay

m09_nearclean_standup.category: near-clean human-style weekly update with one staged run-up
m09_nearclean_standup.expected: minimal edit; 'Here's the thing:' may be cut or kept, but every number, date and dependency stays

m10_nearclean_memoir.category: near-clean personal essay (memoir) with small meaning-bearing words and a lesson ending
m10_nearclean_memoir.expected: few or no changes; no added feelings; small words (more than once, often, badly, still) stay; the closing line may be tightened, not deleted

m11_human_thoreau.category: already-good human literary essay (1854) ending on a one-line aphorism
m11_human_thoreau.expected: few or no changes; the period diction and the closing aphorism are the author's
protected: if that be not a dream
a foot or a foot and a half

m12_human_chesterton.expected: few or no changes; the paradoxes, contrasts and British spelling are the voice

man is a very comic creature
